title: Hardware
heading: Connect and configure your pinball hardware.
intro: Pinball CTL brings your machine's switches, buttons, lights, coils and supported sensors together in one place. Connect your hardware to the ESP32-S3, discover available pins and assign each one a function. Give connections meaningful names, configure their settings and use them throughout your game.
points: Hardware for your whole machine
Configure switches and buttons, individual LEDs, addressable RGB strips, coils and supported sensors and displays.
Find and organise your connections
Reload the available pins from your connected ESP32-S3, including supported expansion hardware where discovery is available. Give connections meaningful names and functions.
Configure and sync
Set safe pin states and appropriate output limits, save your hardware mapping and sync supported settings to the ESP32-S3.
seo_title: Connect and configure your pinball hardware.
seo_description: Pinball CTL brings your machine's switches, buttons, lights, coils and supported sensors together in one place.

title: Rules
heading: Decide what happens in your game.
intro: Create rules that connect machine events to conditions and actions, and review the logic in one visual editor.
points: Connect events and actions
Define what should happen when an input or game event occurs.
Review your rules
Review your rules in one place as the machine evolves.
Connect events to actions
Use the rule editor to connect events, conditions and actions. Keep the logic visible as your machine grows.
Keep supported fast responses on the ESP
Deploy supported hardware rules to the ESP. Flipper and simple lighting responses can run locally while scoring and sound are handled on the Pi.

title: Lighting
heading: Design your playfield lighting.
intro: Place lights on a visual layout, create scenes and preview how they respond to your game before deploying supported configurations.
points: Arrange lights on your playfield
Position fixtures on a visual stage and build scenes around the layout of your playfield.
Create simple effects or full scenes
Use direct event-driven pixel actions for simple feedback, or compose richer scenes for modes and celebrations.
Preview and deploy
Test your ideas visually. Compiled lighting files reduce runtime data, while supported ESP rules execute without a duplicate host action.
seo_description: Design LED lighting for your homebrew pinball machine. Arrange fixtures, preview scenes and deploy lighting configurations to the ESP32.

title: Media
heading: Create content for your backglass and displays.
intro: Build and organise what appears on your machine's screens. Combine text, images, video and Godot scenes, preview the result and choose which displays show each scene.
points: Build display scenes
Bring visual layers and custom fonts together in the Media workspace.
Choose where scenes appear
Choose scene destinations and startup content for configured displays.

title: Live View
heading: Test ideas as you build.
intro: Use a visual playfield to trigger configured inputs and preview lighting. You can develop layouts without a complete cabinet; connected hardware behaviour still needs testing with an ESP.
points: Work with your playfield layout
Use your playfield layout to exercise configured events and inspect how your machine responds.
Test the connected event path
With an ESP connected, simulated inputs travel through the bridge and firmware before reaching host consumers.
Know the limits of a preview
Offline authoring and previews help you iterate. They do not replace testing real electrical outputs and hardware timing.
seo_title: Live Pinball Playfield Preview & Event Testing
seo_description: Preview your pinball playfield and exercise configured events in Live View. Follow the bridge event path while developing your homebrew machine.

title: Performance
heading: Monitor event performance.
intro: See event rates, queue depth and ESP delivery latency so you can investigate slowdowns and protective stops.
points: Compare event rates
Compare incoming events, host processing and ESP confirmations with one- and five-minute charts.
Spot queues and delays
See queued work, the oldest waiting event and delivery latency together, so a busy machine is easier to diagnose.
Review overload status
View overload status and recovery behaviour without changing the firmware’s coil safety limits.
Monitor event delivery
Track incoming events, confirmations, queue depth and delivery latency in the Performance module.
Find useful log messages
Inspect event and service logs without unchanged coil status messages overwhelming the view.
Understand protective stops
Isolated delivery overloads pause activations and recover after cooldown and healthy queues. Repeated overloads and firmware faults remain disarmed.
seo_description: Track event rates, queue depth and ESP32 delivery latency over time. Diagnose delays and understand protective overload handling in pinballCTL.

title: Backup / Restore
heading: Keep a baseline. Restore just what changed.
intro: Export full project baselines or selected components as downloadable ZIP backups. Upload a snapshot to another installation, preview what will change and restore only the parts you choose.
points: Full or selective snapshots
Keep large Media and Audio assets in a baseline, and save frequent small Rules/Lighting updates. Download archives for an off-machine copy or transfer to a compatible installation.
Explicit replacements
Every chosen component is fully replaced; unselected content remains unchanged by default.
Review and recover
Validate archive checksums and dependencies, inspect deletion paths, and retain an automatic pre-restore recovery backup.
seo_title: Pinball Project Import, Export & Backup / Restore
seo_description: Export complete or selective pinball project snapshots, upload compatible ZIP backups and preview component replacements before restoring.
